reason: Method uses futures and leveraged ETFs with intraday minute-bar moving averages and conditional probabilities, not daily-bar rules for US stocks.

setup.rule: Define dip as current price X% below long moving average (e.g. 1000 bars)
setup.quote: I would Define a dip as when current price moves X below an average price that's usually a good indication to buy

entry.rule: Buy when price 2-3% below 1000-bar MA on 1-min or 5-min timeframe
entry.quote: when the price takes a dip say 3% below this very lengthy average there's some research to suggest on my end that it's a good signal that the market might be in a short short-term over reaction

stop.rule: Use low initial position size and build over time with risk management
stop.quote: you just start with a low position size you start building a position over time and you you kind of you kind of just have to do this especially when you're using leverage

exits.rule: Exit when reverts back up to mean; adapt via conditional probabilities
exits.quote: you wait for the trade when you get the trade you enter and then you get out when it reverts back up

sizing.rule: Start small, add leverage on further dips while maintaining risk tools
sizing.quote: once you get an opportunity to buy the dip you could slowly begin to add leverage to that position

market_filter.rule: Use VIX for additional context; avoid RSI
market_filter.quote: yes I will use the vix there's a lot of information in that vix it tells you a lot

ambiguities.issue: Exact % dip, MA length, and holding period not numerically fixed across assets
ambiguities.assumption: Parameters like 2-3% and 1000 bars are representative
